subject.title: [Feature]: Built-in auto-update with configurable schedule, confirmation, and post-update notification

question: Should OpenClaw core own a complete scheduled update-and-notify workflow, and which minimal policy belongs under `update.auto` versus existing cron, approval, continuation, and delivery surfaces?
rationale: The remaining work changes security authority, config contracts, scheduling semantics, cross-channel approval, and restart-state behavior; source inspection can identify reusable primitives but cannot choose these permanent product boundaries.

options.title: Bounded core workflow
options.body: Extend the supervised updater with minimal schedule and consent policy while reusing generic cron, approval, continuation, status, and channel-target contracts.

options.title: Execution primitives only
options.body: Keep core limited to safe update execution and restart status, documenting user-created cron or plugin workflows for approval and notifications.

options.title: Full dedicated update manager
options.body: Add the complete proposed `update.auto` schema and purpose-built scheduler, approval, persistence, changelog, health, and notification subsystem.

recommendation.title: Bounded core workflow
recommendation.body: Extend the supervised updater with minimal schedule and consent policy while reusing generic cron, approval, continuation, status, and channel-target contracts.

likelyOwner.reason: The current updater implementation, config surface, documentation, and prior product review most strongly connect this decision to Peter's recent work.
